briefdescription.para: BitVector default ctor - Creates an empty bitvector.
BitVector ctor - Creates a bitvector of specified number of bits.

detaileddescription.para: All bits are initialized to the specified value.

briefdescription.para: empty - Tests whether there are no bits in this bitvector.
size - Returns the number of bits in this bitvector.
count - Returns the number of bits which are set.
any - Returns true if any bit is set.
all - Returns true if all bits are set.
none - Returns true if none of the bits are set.

memberdef.argsstring: (unsigned Begin, unsigned End, bool Set=true) const
memberdef.name: find_first_in

briefdescription.para: find_first_in - Returns the index of the first set / unset bit, depending on Set, in the range [Begin, End).

detaileddescription.para: Returns -1 if all bits in the range are unset / set.

briefdescription.para: find_last_in - Returns the index of the last set bit in the range [Begin, End).

detaileddescription.para: Returns -1 if all bits in the range are unset.

briefdescription.para: find_first_unset_in - Returns the index of the first unset bit in the range [Begin, End).

detaileddescription.para: Returns -1 if all bits in the range are set.

briefdescription.para: find_last_unset_in - Returns the index of the last unset bit in the range [Begin, End).

detaileddescription.para: Returns -1 if all bits in the range are set.

briefdescription.para: find_first - Returns the index of the first set bit, -1 if none of the bits are set.
find_last - Returns the index of the last set bit, -1 if none of the bits are set.
find_next - Returns the index of the next set bit following the "Prev" bit.

detaileddescription.para: Returns -1 if the next set bit is not found.

briefdescription.para: find_prev - Returns the index of the first set bit that precedes the the bit at PriorTo.

detaileddescription.para: Returns -1 if all previous bits are unset.

briefdescription.para: find_first_unset - Returns the index of the first unset bit, -1 if all of the bits are set.
find_next_unset - Returns the index of the next unset bit following the "Prev" bit.

detaileddescription.para: Returns -1 if all remaining bits are set.

briefdescription.para: find_last_unset - Returns the index of the last unset bit, -1 if all of the bits are set.
find_prev_unset - Returns the index of the first unset bit that precedes the bit at PriorTo.

detaileddescription.para: Returns -1 if all previous bits are set.

briefdescription.para: clear - Removes all bits from the bitvector.
resize - Grow or shrink the bitvector.
set - Efficiently set a range of bits in [I, E)
reset - Efficiently reset a range of bits in [I, E)

Pop one bit from the end of the vector.
Test if any common bits are set.
Intersection, union, disjoint union.
reset - Reset bits that are set in RHS. Same as *this &= ~RHS.
test - Check if (This - RHS) is zero.

briefdescription.para: setBitsInMask - Add '1' bits from Mask to this vector.
clearBitsInMask - Clear any bits in this vector that are set in Mask.
setBitsNotInMask - Add a bit to this vector for every '0' bit in Mask.
clearBitsNotInMask - Clear a bit in this vector for every '0' bit in Mask.
Return the size (in bytes) of the bit vector.
Perform a logical left shift of Count words by moving everything Count words to the right in memory.

detaileddescription.para: While confusing, words are stored from least significant at Bits[0] to most significant at Bits[NumWords-1]. A logical shift left, however, moves the current least significant bit to a higher logical index, and fills the previous least significant bits with 0. Thus, we actually need to move the bytes of the memory to the right, not to the left. Example: Words = [0xBBBBAAAA, 0xDDDDFFFF, 0x00000000, 0xDDDD0000] represents a BitVector where 0xBBBBAAAA contain the least significant bits. So if we want to shift the BitVector left by 2 words, we need to turn this into 0x00000000 0x00000000 0xBBBBAAAA 0xDDDDFFFF by using a memmove which moves right, not left.

briefdescription.para: Perform a logical right shift of Count words by moving those words to the left in memory.
